title: SHISA3 Reprograms Tumor‐Associated Macrophages Toward an Antitumoral Phenotype and Enhances Cancer Immunotherapy
authors: Shimeng Zhang; Bingbing Yu; Chunjie Sheng; Chen Yao; Yang Liu; Jing Wang; Qi Zeng; Yizhi Mao; Jinxin...
id: Matched: SHISA3 Promotes Macrophage Polarize Toward an M1 Phenotype
abstract: This study investigated SHISA3's role in reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages. SHISA3 enhances cancer immunotherapy by promoting an antitumoral macrophage phenotype and boosting T cell responses.

title: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced Macrophage Activation and Signal Transduction in the Absence of Src-Family Kinases Hck, Fgr, and Lyn
authors: Fanying Meng; Clifford A. Lowell
abstract: This study investigated LPS-induced macrophage activation in mice lacking Src-family kinases Hck, Fgr, and Lyn. Macrophages from these mice showed no major defects in LPS-induced activation, indicating these kinases are not obligatory for LPS signaling.

title: Macrophage Polarization: Different Gene Signatures in M1(LPS+) vs. Classically and M2(LPS–) vs. Alternatively Activated Macrophages
authors: Marco Orecchioni, Yanal Ghosheh, Akula Bala Pramod, Klaus Ley
abstract: This study compared gene expression in *in vivo* M1/M2 macrophages with *in vitro* classically/alternatively activated macrophages. The findings indicate that *in vivo* M1/M2 polarization is not equivalent to *in vitro* activation states.

title: Genome-wide siRNA screen of genes regulating the LPS-induced NF-κB and TNF-α responses in mouse macrophages
authors: Ning Li, Samuel Katz, Bhaskar Dutta, Zachary L. Benet, Jing Sun, Iain D.C. Fraser
abstract: A genome-wide siRNA screen identified genes regulating LPS-induced NF-κB and TNF-α responses in mouse macrophages. This study provides a resource for analyzing gene function in this key inflammatory pathway.

authors: Hwa-Jin Chung; Wonil Koh; Won Kyung Kim; Joon-Shik Shin; Jinho Lee; Sang Kook Lee; In-Hyuk Ha
id: Matched: 3.3. Effect of Shinbaro3 on Inflammatory Mediator Expression
abstract: Shinbaro3 was studied for its anti-inflammatory effects in LPS-stimulated macrophages. It was found to inhibit inflammation by downregulating the TLR4 signaling pathway.

title: Analysis of the transcriptional networks underpinning the activation of murine macrophages by inflammatory mediators
authors: Sobia Raza, Mark W. Barnett, Zohar Barnett-Itzhaki, Ido Amit, David A. Hume, Tom C. Freeman
abstract: Transcriptomic data was analyzed to understand macrophage activation by inflammatory mediators. The LPS response can be divided into more co-regulated gene subsets than previously thought.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-mediated macrophage polarization, conserved pathogenesis, and implications for peripheral neuropathy: a systematic review
authors: Leah Elson; Niels Eijkelkamp; J. Henk Coert
abstract: This systematic review synthesized evidence for a conserved lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-mediated pathogenic mechanism across diverse tissues and evaluated its potential relevance to peripheral neuropathy

title: Investigation of microRNAs in mouse macrophage responses to lipopolysaccharide-stimulation by combining gene expression with microRNA-target information
authors: Chia-Chun Chiu, Wei-Sheng Wu
abstract: This study integrated gene expression and miRNA-target data to analyze mouse macrophage responses to LPS. The findings suggest miRNAs are important regulators of LPS-induced innate immune responses in macrophages.

title: Genome-wide siRNA screen of genes regulating the LPS-induced TNF-α response in human macrophages
authors: Jing Sun; Samuel Katz; Bhaskar Dutta; Ze Wang; Iain D.C. Fraser
abstract: A genome-wide siRNA screen identified genes regulating the LPS-induced TNF-α response in human macrophages. Novel hits broadly affect innate inflammatory responses to microbial stimuli.

title: Cooperative and distinct functions of MK2 and MK3 in the regulation of the macrophage transcriptional response to lipopolysaccharide
authors: Christian Ehlting; Julia Rex; Ute Albrecht; René Deenen; Christopher Tiedje; Karl Köhrer; Oliver Saw...
id: Matched: Analysis of the differential regulation of LPS-inducible gene expressi
abstract: MK2 and MK3 were studied for their roles in regulating macrophage responses to LPS. They cooperatively and distinctly control inflammatory gene expression, with MK3 also negatively regulating IFN-β in MK2's absence.

title: Lipopolysaccharide from biofilm-forming Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 induces macrophage hyperinflammatory responses
authors: Sufei Wang; Dandan Xiang; Fangbing Tian; Ming Ni
abstract: Biofilm-forming *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* LPS was studied for its effect on macrophage polarization. This LPS induced hyperinflammatory responses and increased bacterial growth in macrophages compared to planktonic LPS.

title: SRSF3 Knockdown Inhibits Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Inflammatory Response in Macrophages
authors: Yu Fu; Yanjing Wang; Luyao Zhang; Tianliu He; Weiye Shi; Xueling Guo; Yingze Wang
id: Matched: 3.2. The Expression of SRSF3 Is Upregulated in Lipopolysaccharide-Stim
abstract: SRSF3 expression was studied in inflammatory macrophages and found to be increased. Downregulating SRSF3 inhibited inflammation by deactivating NFκB and altering MD2 splicing.

title: Shisa3 brakes resistance to EGFR-TKIs in lung adenocarcinoma by suppressing cancer stem cell properties
authors: Jiahui Si; Yuanyuan Ma; Ji Wang Bi; Ying Xiong; Chao Lv; Shaolei Li; Nan Wu; Yue Yang
id: Matched: Targeting shisa3-regulated signaling attenuated EGFR-TKI resistance
abstract: Shisa3 was studied as a suppressor of EGFR-TKI resistance and cancer stem cell properties in lung adenocarcinoma. Low shisa3 expression promotes resistance by enhancing CSC traits via FGFR/AKT/mTOR signaling.

authors: Stephen J. Bush; Mary E. B. McCulloch; Zofia M. Lisowski; Charity Muriuki; Emily L. Clark; Rachel Yo...
abstract: This study analyzed the transcriptional response of sheep macrophages to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and compared it to other mammalian species. A conserved transcriptional network was found, but large animals and rodents differed in their metabolic responses to LPS.

title: Transducin-like enhancer of split 3 protects against lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation through DEAD-box helicase 5–activating transcription factor 1–protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit 5A signaling
authors: Di Fan; Yi Zhong; Yin Dong; Meng Du; Kai Huang; Xiaoguang Li
id: Matched: TLE3 protects against LPS-induced acute multi-organ injury and systemi
abstract: Transducin-like enhancer of split 3 (TLE3) was studied for its role in lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation. TLE3 mitigates this inflammation by modulating the DEAD-box helicase 5–activating transcription factor 1–protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit 5A signaling pathway.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-Activated Macrophages Suppress Cellular Senescence and Promote Rejuvenation in Human Dermal Fibroblasts
authors: Hiroyuki Inagawa; Chie Kohchi; Miyuki Uehiro; Gen-Ichiro Soma
abstract: LPS-activated macrophages were studied for their effect on senescent human dermal fibroblasts. Their secretions suppressed senescence and partially rejuvenated aged fibroblasts.

title: Pro-Inflammatory Role of S1P3 in Macrophages
authors: Jae-Yeong Heo; Dong-Soon Im
abstract: This study investigated the role of S1P3 in primary macrophages. S1P3 was found to promote the induction of inflammatory genes, suggesting it as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Lipopolysaccharide regulation of antiinflammatory tristetraprolin family and proinflammatory gene expression in mouse macrophages
authors: Heping Cao
id: Matched: Effect of LPS on TTP homologue gene expression
abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) was studied for its effects on tristetraprolin (TTP) family and proinflammatory gene expression in mouse macrophages. LPS increased TTP, TNF, and COX2 mRNA but had minimal impact on other TTP homologues and proinflammatory cytokine genes.

title: LncRNA HOTAIR regulates lipopolysaccharide-induced cytokine expression and inflammatory response in macrophages
authors: Monira Obaid; S. M. Nashir Udden; Paromita Deb; Nadine Shihabeddin; Md. Hasan Zaki; Subhrangsu S. Ma...
id: Matched: Cell culture and treatment with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)
abstract: LncRNA HOTAIR's role in LPS-induced inflammation in macrophages was studied. HOTAIR promotes NF-κB activation and cytokine expression by facilitating IκBα degradation.

title: Dynamic nucleosome redistribution and increases in nucleosome sensitivity underpin THP-1 macrophage response to LPS
authors: Jane M Benoit, Brandon D Buck, Mahdi Khadem, Hank W Bass, Jonathan H Dennis *
abstract: Nucleosome distribution and MNase sensitivity were assessed across macrophage promoters after LPS stimulation. A subset of immune gene promoters showed transient nucleosome redistribution, while MNase sensitivity changes were largely uncoupled from gene expression.

title: SENP3 facilitates M1 macrophage polarization via the HIF-1α/PKM2 axis in lipopolysaccharide-induced acute lung injury
authors: Shuangjun He; Chenyu Fan; Yiming Ji; Qian Su; Feng Zhao; Cuiying Xie; Xuelian Chen; Yang Zhang; Yi C...
id: Matched: SENP3 deficiency dampens the LPS-induced inflammatory response through
abstract: SENP3 deficiency inhibits M1 macrophage polarization and pro-inflammatory cytokine production in LPS-induced acute lung injury. This occurs via the HIF-1α/PKM2 axis, suggesting SENP3 as a therapeutic target.

title: Selection of reliable reference genes for the normalisation of gene expression levels following time course LPS stimulation of murine bone marrow derived macrophages
authors: Akane Tanaka, Joyce To, Bronwyn O’Brien, Sheila Donnelly, Maria Lund
abstract: This study assessed the stability of eight common reference genes in LPS-stimulated murine macrophages. It found that some traditional genes are unreliable, and identified two new, stable reference genes for accurate gene expression analysis.
